Technical & Consumer Questions Answered • v0.5.0

Frequently Asked Questions

Clear, honest answers about Dual-Layer Microsoft Azure Artifact Signing, why our universal installer targets 64-bit x64 and ARM64 (skipping extinct IA-64 and 32-bit x86 host OS builds while still supporting legacy 32-bit app payloads), plain-English setup tiers, accessibility, and our permanent Community == Premier pledge.

Part 1 • Downloads, Authenticode Signing & Supported Processors

Code Signing, CPU Detection & Architecture Choices

1. Are RaggieSoft Installer Studio downloads cryptographically signed for Windows SmartScreen & UAC?

Yes! Starting in v0.4.5, 100% of our official downloads and inner binaries are cryptographically Authenticode-signed via Microsoft Azure Artifact Signing under verified Public Trust identity (Michael Ragsdale) with RFC 3161 SHA-256 timestamps (http://timestamp.acs.microsoft.com).

Our build pipeline signs every inner suite executable first (InstallerStudio.exe, instbuild.exe, SetupWizard.exe, msiprism.exe, and RaggieSoftHelp.exe), then Dual-Layer signs both the inner .msi database and outer Universal Setup.exe launchers—verified against WinVerifyTrust (signtool verify /pa) before upload.

2. I don't know whether my Windows PC is AMD64 (x64) or ARM64. Which file do I download?

Either of our two universal buttons works on both Intel/AMD x64 and Snapdragon / Windows on ARM ARM64 computers automatically:

  • Smart Web Setup (raggiesoft-installer-studio-setup.exe, ~790 KB): Queries IsWow64Process2 at launch (piercing Windows 11 Prism emulation in under 0.1ms), downloads only your processor's native signed installer over HTTPS, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and runs it natively.
  • Full Offline Universal Installer (raggiesoft-installer-studio-offline-setup.exe, ~3.6 MB): Packs both signed x64 and ARM64 native installers inside one portable file for offline or air-gapped PCs and USB drives.

3. Why are IA-64 (Itanium) and 32-bit x86 host OS builds skipped?

Every supported Windows desktop, laptop, and workstation in late 2026 runs a 64-bit operating system kernel (IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_AMD64 0x8664 or IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_ARM64 0xAA64):

  • IA-64 (Intel Itanium) is museum hardware: Intel ended the Itanium hardware lifecycle in 2021, Microsoft ended mainstream Windows Itanium support over a decade ago, and modern MSVC / Windows 11 SDK compilers removed IA64 backend targets completely. Better yet, skipping Itanium lets instbuild.exe strictly guard against one of Windows Installer's oldest traps—never emitting PID_TEMPLATE = Intel64;1033 (which meant Itanium and causes msiexec on Intel Core and AMD Ryzen PCs to reject the MSI!), using strictly x64;1033 and Arm64;1033 instead.
  • 32-bit x86 Windows OS is retired: Windows 11 has never shipped a 32-bit operating system image, and 32-bit Windows 10 reached formal End of Support in October 2025. Using a pure 64-bit x64 outer universal stub avoids relying on optional 32-bit WOW64 subsystems on hardened Windows images while booting seamlessly under Windows 11 Prism on ARM64.

4. Can a 64-bit Installer Studio still package legacy 32-bit applications (such as classic Visual Basic 6.0 programs)?

Yes! Skipping 32-bit host OS builds for our IDE and compiler does not prevent a 64-bit instbuild.exe from packaging legacy 32-bit payload applications that run on Windows 11 x64 and ARM64 via SysWOW64. Our upcoming v0.8.0 milestone includes a dedicated Visual Basic 6.0 (.vbp) Importer (built for our own pre-AI utility StoreTrainer) that emits standard 32-bit payload MSI metadata (Intel;1033 routing to Program Files (x86)) and zero-elevation Reg-Free COM side-by-side manifests—all from the native 64-bit IDE.

Part 2 • Setup Types, Inclusion Tiers & Accessibility

Plain-English Authoring, Dark Mode & Zero Dependencies

5. What is "Included In" (Minimal, Typical, Complete) vs. Windows Installer InstallLevel?

Raw Windows Installer databases use an obscure integer column called Feature.Level compared against an INSTALLLEVEL property—forcing authors to guess what numbers like 1, 3, 100, or 200 actually do.

Starting in v0.4.4, RaggieSoft Installer Studio replaces raw numbers in the IDE with plain-English Included In tiers: Minimal / Compact & All Setups (minimal), Typical / Express & Complete (typical), Complete Only / Optional in Custom (complete), and Hidden (hidden). And in v0.5.0, authors will also be able to pick classic Windows 95-style Setup Types (Typical, Compact, Complete, Custom) or define their own named [SetupType.*] presets!

6. Does Installer Studio require .NET, WebView2, Java, or Electron on my PC or my users' PCs?

Zero. All five binaries (InstallerStudio.exe, instbuild.exe, SetupWizard.exe, msiprism.exe, and RaggieSoftHelp.exe) are compiled as static /MT native Win32 C++20 executables calling only stock DLLs built into every copy of Windows 11 (msi.dll, cabinet.dll, gdiplus.dll, winhttp.dll, and Msftedit.dll). If your packaged app needs .NET, WebView2, or VC++, declare a [Prerequisite.*] block and SetupWizard.exe will install it automatically before your MSI runs.

7. How does Dark Mode, High Contrast, and Screen-Reader Accessibility work inside Setup.exe?

Stock Windows Installer internal dialogs still paint 1990s blinding white GDI headers even when Windows 11 is in Dark Mode. Our SetupWizard.exe external UI subclasses real Win32 push buttons, option cards, checkboxes, and 32-bit ARGB SelectionTree controls so native UI Automation roles remain intact for Narrator, NVDA, and JAWS, flips between Light and Dark Mode live in under 16ms on WM_SETTINGCHANGE(ImmersiveColorSet), honors Windows Contrast Themes (SPI_GETHIGHCONTRAST), and generates HTML5 VPAT 2.5 reports via --emit-vpat.

Part 3 • Licensing, Enterprise IT & AI Coding Agents

Community == Premier Parity, Silent Deployment & AI Specs

8. Does Community Edition really have 100% feature parity with Premier—with zero watermarks?

Yes, permanently. Community Edition unlocks every single MSI table, Pre-MSI Runtime Prerequisite, 64-bit .MSM Merge Module weaver, Universal Single-EXE packager, AeroWizard, VPAT 2.5 generator, and CLI command with zero locked views and zero visible watermarks. Every compiled Setup.exe and Product.msi carries 100% your own Manufacturer and ProductName in VERSIONINFO.

9. Can IT administrators deploy silently or extract the standalone .msi for Intune / Group Policy?

Yes! Every generated installer is backed by a genuine relational Windows Installer database. Run <App>-setup.exe /s INSTALLDIR="C:\Apps\MyApp" for completely silent prerequisite + MSI installation (with configurable SilentRebootExitCode), or run <App>-setup.exe --extract-msi C:\Temp\Out (works on both per-arch and Universal Offline EXEs!) to extract the signed .msi alongside .mst Transforms and .msp Patches.

10. How do AI coding agents use Installer Studio—and what defines v1.0.0 GA?

.rsip projects and .rsis suites are diff-friendly plain-text INI manifests whose comments and @include headers survive GUI saves byte-for-byte. Coding agents read our compiler-emitted /llms-full.txt and SKILL.md specs and lint manifests in under a millisecond via instbuild.exe --validate --diagnostics=json. Version 1.0.0 GA will ship once 100% of RaggieSoft's own Windows desktop apps, classic VB6 tools, interactive novels, and audio archives are packaged, signed, and updated exclusively with Installer Studio.
